readout_other: Compound action potentials of alpha, beta and gamma fibre groups recorded from the sciatic nerve
direction_notes: Focused ultrasound reversibly or irreversibly blocked conduction in the sciatic nerve; smaller myelinated fibres (gamma, then beta) were blocked before larger alpha fibres, and repeated ultrasound produced cumulative, increasing depression of conduction.

exposures.label: Focused ultrasound irradiation of frog sciatic nerve

timing.protocol_description: The ultrasound (2.7 megacycles per sec.) was administered in pulses of 0.14-1.2 sec. duration, with a 2-3 sec. interval between pulses. In each experiment the flux of ultrasound (pulse width and train length) was increased gradually until a level was reached which would affect conduction of impulses; depending on the effect desired, a pulse width of 0.5-0.8 sec. and a train length of 1-20 pulses were usually employed.

source_quotes.n_subjects: Effects similar to this were observed in experiments on 15 different nerves.
source_quotes.exposures[0].unspecified_domain.isppa_w_: Before each experiment the output of the transducer was calibrated to yield an intensity of 1,150 watts per square centimeter at the focal region."

flags.reason: Paper states only an undifferentiated 'intensity' (1,150 W/cm^2) calibrated at the focal region in saline; it does not specify spatial-peak pulse-average vs. temporal-average, and the nerve itself was covered in liquid petrolatum rather than saline during exposure, so the domain of this calibration value is uncertain.
Only an inter-pulse interval (2-3 s) and train lengths (1-20 pulses) are given; no explicit repetition rate or duty cycle is stated.
